Source: GOS 2026 Our BSc (Hons) Animal Management (Pet Behaviour and Welfare) blends scientific theory with hands-on experience to prepare you for careers in animal behaviour, training and welfare. With UK pet ownership rising and demand for qualified professionals growing, you’ll develop the essential practical and academic skills needed to succeed. From working with a diverse range of species to gaining real clinical insight in our Pet Behaviour Clinic, you’ll graduate confident and career ready. Animal Behaviour and Training Council This degree course is recognised by the Animal Behaviour and Training Council (ABTC), for the roles of animal trainer, animal training instructor, animal behaviour technician, and clinical animal behaviourist. As a graduate you'll also be eligible for provisional membership of the Association of Pet Behaviour Counsellors. Find out more about studying Animal Management at ARU in this short video. Gain hands-on experience with a wide range of species from day one Learn in our on-site Pet Behaviour Clinic, observing and supporting real consultations Benefit from expert teaching, guest lectures and connect through strong industry links Study a holistic curriculum covering behaviour, nutrition, health, welfare, ethics, legislation and business Recognised by the ABTC, with eligibility for Associate Membership of the Association of Pet Behaviour Counsellors Gain real-world experience through field trips to rescue centres, wildlife organisations and other institutions Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers The pet behaviour and welfare course has prepared me within my line of work, providing me with a crucial insight towards a working clinic and authentic cases. Dani Chabot, BSc (Hons) Animal Management (Pet Behaviour and Welfare), Canine Behaviour Coach at Dogs Trust, helping pet dogs and recently rehomed rescue dogs develop a bond with their owners Our course’s recognition from the ABTC means you’ll gain the most up-to-date animal training and behaviour knowledge and skills. By studying BSc (Hons) Animal Management (Pet Behaviour and Welfare), you’ll be equipped with a wide range of practical and professional skills. You’ll learn animal handling and husbandry, behaviour assessment and training, and gain knowledge of health, welfare and nutrition. Our ABTC-recognised course ensures you’ll gain the most up-to-date training and behaviour expertise, while also developing research, problem-solving and communication skills, preparing you for a successful career in pet behaviour, training and welfare. What can you do with an Animal Management (Pet Behaviour and Welfare) degree? Through comprehensive animal science training, you’ll gain the practical skills and scientific knowledge to access a wide range of exciting careers within the animal industry. This course will open doors to exciting roles, whether you see yourself as a pet behaviourist, supporting animal welfare and rescue, working in veterinary care, inspiring through education or contributing to research and consultancy. With this degree, you’ll be ready to make an impact across the companion animal sector and beyond. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our MSc Animal Welfare and Conservation or MSc Conservation Education and Engagement . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Where have other Animal Management (Pet Behaviour and Welfare) graduates worked? As well as the roles mentioned above, previous graduates have found success in related fields such as animal nutrition, animal welfare, nutrition company sales, and veterinary pharmaceutical and equipment supplies. You might also progress to vet school. From ARU student to wildlife presenter Animal Management graduate Amye uses the knowledge she gained at ARU to help others understand the importance of welfare and conservation. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our pet behaviour and welfare graduates leave ready to practice as clinicians, equipped with real-world experience and industry-recognised expertise. Debbie Emmerson, Pet Behaviour and Welfare lead You’ll start by learning about the fundamentals of animal management, covering biology, ethics, and essential practical and professional skills. In years 2-3, as well as building on your knowledge of these core topics, you’ll focus on animal behaviour, training and welfare as they pertain to companion animals, and develop the specific professional skills you need to work as a pet trainer or behaviourist. You’ll round off your degree with an independent research project on a relevant topic of your choice, drawing on everything you’ve learned over the three years. What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. How is Animal Management (Pet Welfare and Behaviour) assessed? We'll assess your progress in a number of ways to ensure practical and academic competence, including assignments, reports, written examinations, observed structured practical examinations, observed structured clinical examinations, oral presentations, debates, and your dissertation. What equipment will I need? You’ll need a laptop, along with standard safety equipment for outdoor work. This includes steel toe-capped boots or wellingtons, long-sleeved overalls and a waterproof jacket and trousers. The estimated cost is between £100 and £250. You’ll also need notebook and paper for note taking, pens, pencils folders and a scientific calculator. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in optional animal and conservation trips, both locally and overseas. Please note that these trips are self-funded at your own expense. Most full-time UK students can apply for a Maintenance Loan to help cover living costs. More about maintenance loans . We also have a range of offers to help with the cost of living . Postgraduate MSc Crop Production Learn how to tackle food insecurity and climate change through real-world research and transformative learning. Become an innovator at ARU in Writtle. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event MSc 2 years part-time MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 Location Writtle Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), or 16 months (January starts). The part-time option takes two years. 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 With rising global population, climate change and increasing pressure on land use, the need for sustainable crop production has never been more critical. This MSc equips you with advanced knowledge and practical skills across field, protected and controlled environment crop production systems. Through access to our research glasshouse, working farm, commercial grower visits and industry speakers, you’ll gain practical insight into modern crop production and the challenges of future food security. Why ARU? Study on a specialist land-based campus with research glasshouses and a working farm Learn from experts in sustainable agriculture, horticulture and controlled environment agriculture Develop practical skills through fieldwork, commercial visits and applied research Explore the supply chain from production and postharvest to market Engage with industry partners and guest speakers driving innovation Build advanced research and analytical skills to solve real-world challenges Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers ARU Writtle’s specialised education empowered me to lead high-tech facilities, managing international commercial production alongside world-class agronomists globally. Patrick Phiri, MSc Crop Production graduate Prepare to lead innovation in agriculture and horticulture. You'll graduate with the knowledge and practical skills needed to address the challenges facing modern crop production. Career opportunities exist across commercial agriculture, horticulture, controlled environment agriculture, agritech businesses, and organisations involved in wholesale, retail and import/export. The course also provides a strong foundation for research careers and future study in crop production and related disciplines. What can you do with a Crop Production degree? A Crop Production degree can open doors to a wide range of careers across agriculture, horticulture and agri-tech. You might work in commercial crop production, protected cropping systems, agronomy, technical advisory roles, research and development, supply chain management, quality assurance, or the fresh produce sector. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. Where have previous graduates worked? Graduates have progressed into roles across commercial crop production, protected cropping, agronomy, technical advisory services, research, supply chain management and further postgraduate study. Career destinations span both the agriculture and horticulture sectors in the UK and internationally. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules We combine scientific knowledge, practical experience and industry engagement to prepare future leaders in crop production. Dr Kami Baghalian, Course Director Gain an understanding of crop production today and in the future. By studying sustainable crop production, postharvest management, controlled environment agriculture, strategic management and the global forces shaping food systems, you'll develop a broad and integrated understanding of crop production across field, protected and controlled environment systems. Through practical sessions, case studies, commercial site visits and applied research, you'll develop the skills to analyse complex challenges and design evidence-based solutions. You'll complete your Master's with a substantial research project on a topic relevant to your interests and career aspirations. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Sustainable Crop Production (15 credits) Applied Research (Methods) for Managers (15 credits) Cropping Systems and Innovations (15 credits) Strategic Management (15 credits) Into ARU Postharvest Systems Management (15 credits) Sustainable Global Business Management and Circular Economics (15 credits) Controlled Environment Agriculture (15 credits) Food Security and Sustainable Farm Management (15 credits) Postgraduate Major Project (60 credits) Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. What equipment will I need? It’s advisable to have the following equipment: A digital camera/camera app on your phone is useful for taking photos during visits and practical work when appropriate Suitable sturdy footwear for visits and estate work Waterproof clothing Lab coat (optional as these can be provided) Laptop or tablet (essential) How is Crop Production assessed? Assessment is designed to help you apply knowledge and skills to real-world crop production challenges. You'll be assessed through a range of methods, including reports, presentations, case studies, research assignments and data analysis exercises. You'll also complete a substantial independent dissertation project, allowing you to investigate a topic relevant to your academic or professional interests. Who teaches Crop Production at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Kami Baghalian Senior Lecturer in Crop Production Dr Robin Gowers Senior Lecturer Dr Anya Perera Deputy Head of School Dr Anne Mumbi Senior Lecturer in Agribusiness for Sustainable Production Dr Christos Gerofotis Lecturer Ruvini Ranasingha Lecturer in Commercial Production (Fresh Produce) Facilities Here at ARU Writtle , you'll benefit from specialist teaching, research and practical facilities. These include research glasshouses, a working farm, regenerative agriculture demonstration areas, modern laboratories and dedicated teaching spaces. Together, these facilities provide opportunities to explore crop production across field, protected and controlled environment systems. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Course durations may vary slightly and you can contact us for more information. Course content and modules remain the same. 2 years part-time You can choose to study this course part-time, and start in September or January. The course durations vary slightly: 2 years (September starts) or 28 months (January starts). Course content and modules remain the same. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Whether you're a civil engineer looking to develop your management expertise, new to construction management, or aspiring to progress to a management position, this MSc will equip you with the knowledge, skills and confidence to succeed. You'll develop your own leadership management style while consolidating your skills through an independent research or work-based project. Our modules give you a comprehensive understanding of the role of leadership and management throughout the construction process. From leading and managing multidisciplinary teams to addressing complex construction-related challenges, you'll develop the strategic, technical and professional capabilities to manage projects effectively. Accredited by CIOB Our Construction and Civil Engineering MSc degree is accredited by The Chartered Association of Building (CIOB) . Once you've completed three years of on-the-job experience, you'll be eligible to apply for Chartered Status with CIOB. Why ARU? Learn to plan and manage construction and civil engineering projects and project teams Develop your own leadership and management style Study on campus or by distance learning Apply for Chartered Status with CIOB after three years of work experience Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers I dreamt of a future me making a positive impact in the world and ARU made this dream a reality. Nathaniel Acquah Build the knowledge, confidence and practical expertise to advance your career. Construction and civil engineering managers oversee the planning and delivery of every stage of their projects. They make sure projects are delivered on time, within budgets and to the required quality standards. On this MSc, you'll develop a strong understanding of leadership and management across the project lifecycle. You'll gain skills to lead teams, solve complex project challenges and make informed management decisions. It's ideal if you're already in a management position, or looking to progress into one. What can you do with a Construction and Civil Engineering Management degree? This Master's course prepares you to progress from technical engineering into leadership, project delivery, and strategic roles across the construction and civil engineering sectors. As a graduate, you'll be well-equipped for careers as a project manager, site or contracts manager, or a construction manager, where you’ll oversee planning, budgets, and delivery of infrastructure and building projects. You could also explore roles in civil engineering and consultancy. This course also opens opportunities for roles in new and emerging areas, such as sustainability consultant, environmental engineer, and procurement or supply chain manager, focusing on green construction and contract strategy. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a PhD programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. Where have previous graduates worked? Our graduates typically go on to careers in construction firms, engineering and design consultancies, property development companies, and infrastructure organisations around the world. Others find employment in public-sector bodies such as local authorities and utilities. Many graduates progress into professional and managerial roles within a relatively short time after completing their degrees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules The course will develop the expertise required to manage complex projects and deliver sustainable built environments worldwide. Dr Joseph K Ofori-Kuragu Learn how to plan and control projects effectively using IT, gain an understanding of the economic, legal and political influences on built environment firms, and find out how to adapt and re-use existing buildings for new purposes, and the benefits and implications of doing so. You'll learn the key principles and practices of management, people management, HR policy and practices, and how to motivate and develop your colleagues. You'll also learn how to manage procurement and supply chains, as well as sustainability and environmental considerations. You'll gain an understanding of research design methods, then put them into practice by conducting a major research project from start to finish with support from an appropriate member of staff. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time Distance learning MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Project Planning and Control (15 credits) Management Theory (15 credits) Sustainability and Environmental Management (15 credits) Management Practice (15 credits) Economic, Political and Legal Framework (15 credits) Structural Adaptation and Re-use of Buildings (15 credits) Procurement and Supply Chain Management (15 credits) Research Design and Methods (15 credits) Dissertation (60 credits) Into ARU Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. Distance learning There'll be times when you'll study two modules simultaneously during a trimester. Our tutors will help you to manage your workload and assessment deadlines. Please contact us to discuss the pacing of this course and the options available to you. Email [email protected] or call 01245 686707. Find out more about this course on our Distance Learning website . Who teaches Construction and Civil Engineering Management at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Christian Henjewele Senior Lecturer Dr Hussein Adebayo Ibrahim Senior Lecturer Negar Ahmadpoor Lecturer Dr Joseph Ofori-Kuragu Senior Lecturer Graham Terry Senior Lecturer Practitioner Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students .
